classification.difficultyReason: Model committee selection without replacement, calculate both girls and at least one girl using disjoint paths or a complement, then form their conditional ratio. These linked steps must be selected without intermediate prompts.

content.prompt:
A small committee of two is formed from a group of 4 boys and 8 girls.
If at least one of the members is a girl, what is the probability that both are girls?

answer.worked:
A probability tree is useful here. Let $G$ denote a girl and $B$ a boy. The second selection is made without replacement.

$$\begin{align*}P(GG)&=\frac{8}{12}\times\frac{7}{11}=\frac{14}{33}\\P(GB)&=\frac{8}{12}\times\frac{4}{11}=\frac{8}{33}\\P(BG)&=\frac{4}{12}\times\frac{8}{11}=\frac{8}{33}\\P(\text{at least one girl})&=\frac{14}{33}+\frac{8}{33}+\frac{8}{33}=\frac{30}{33}\\P(\text{both girls}\mid\text{at least one girl})&=\frac{P(\text{both girls})}{P(\text{at least one girl})}\\P(\text{both girls}\mid\text{at least one girl})&=\frac{14/33}{30/33}=\frac{7}{15}\end{align*}$$
